Grower/breeder here, every plant is an individual and will treat every person as such. I like to explain it like dog breeds because everyone can relate so take german shepherds for example which from far away all look the same. As you look closer you can see differences in their fur patterns, some have floppy ears, others pointier noses, etc. and when you really get to interact with them you then get to see what kind of dog you have on your hands. You can see if they're lazy, energetic, playful, aggressive, etc. and only once you know them like that will you know if they're suitable for you or not. If you think of cannabis the same way with the obvious exception of needing outright numbers to find that suitable plant instead of having the option of plant school to iron out imperfections you'll enjoy a life long hunt for that perfect plant and will find many a strain that you fall in love with along the way.

Also don't buy into thc percentages, ratios, etc. because at an individual level they're nothing more than numbers people can put on paper as a sales pitch. It's all about the user experience and the only proof you will ever need of that is that thc from an indica the same as the thc from a sativa yet the highs are wildly different. Higher thc percentage might mean more raw strength but it comes at the cost of other cannabinoids that make up the totality of the high so what you make up for in quantity you lose in quality. Go with your own experiences and never buy into the hype because once you do you start going down a path that won't be true to your needs or desires and you'll have predictably unsuitable results such as breeders trying to get the highest thc percentage possible. Doing that will result in people flipping their shit as there won't be the cannabinoids to counter the straight hit of thc they'd normally have gotten from cannabis a generation ago before people demanded labs spit out numbers on paper that we can use to judge a plant.
